content_blocks.label: lead_paragraph
content_blocks.text: Tensions escalated this week as protests erupted in several cities over proposed police reform legislation, which advocates say is too weak to address systemic racism and brutality.

content_blocks.label: body_paragraph_1
content_blocks.text: The bill, known as the 'Community Safety Act,' seeks to limit use-of-force policies and increase transparency in police departments, but many activists argue it falls short of what is needed to rebuild trust between law enforcement and minority communities.

content_blocks.label: body_paragraph_2
content_blocks.text: Protest organizers chanted slogans such as 'No justice, no peace' and demanded more comprehensive reforms, including the abolition of qualified immunity for police officers.

content_blocks.label: body_paragraph_3
content_blocks.text: City Councilor James Thompson expressed his frustration, saying, 'These reforms are a step in the right direction, but they must go further to truly make our communities safe.'

content_blocks.label: body_paragraph_4
content_blocks.text: The demonstrations highlight ongoing debates about policing and accountability, with no clear resolution in sight.

content_blocks.label: pull_quote
content_blocks.text: ‘Our streets are not safe until we have real change, not just window dressing.’ - Protest Organizer Maria Garcia
